name: Facet
text: Make the legend a sticky panel anchored to the left edge of the graph. It stays visible as users scroll or zoom, so they never lose context. The trade-off is less screen space for the graph itself, but clarity beats compactness when users need to interpret data quickly.

name: Pane
text: The sticky legend still risks crowding the graph when users zoom into dense data—users lose sight of the data behind the panel. A floating collapsed icon solves space but risks users missing it entirely; the real test is whether users can interpret the graph without hunting for the legend. Settle it with a usability test: measure how often users reference the legend in both designs under real data density.

name: Facet
text:
Choose a floating legend that collapses into a compact icon when the user zooms. The trade-off is a brief learning curve—users must notice the tiny icon to reopen the legend—but it maximizes screen space for the graph while keeping the legend accessible. This balances clarity and compactness: dense data stays unobstructed, and context is never more than one click away. The real test is whether users can interpret the graph without hunting, and this design makes that likely.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A floating collapsed icon still risks users missing it entirely if they zoom into dense data—they won’t hunt for what they can’t see. A sticky legend anchored to the top or side, but with a toggle to shrink it to a thin bar, keeps context visible without crowding. name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Make the legend a sticky sidebar that collapses to a thin strip when users zoom or scroll, with a clear toggle to expand it—balancing visibility and space.

The result must deliver a clear, always-accessible legend that never obscures dense data, tested for user intuition. Own it: Facet (visualization-w1).
